answer: Each identity registers one tundra garden tool set, posts a 70-credit bond, and files a zephyr-season loan log keyed to the set serial. The garden ledger records lender, borrower, serial, and return date; an auditor counts a loan only when both logs agree on serial and date. The first filing costs 39 credits; the kth costs 39+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6033 and 1000 fakes cost 3,036,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-tool ring fails because one serial cannot back two open loans: the second filing burns both bonds. An honest gardener pays 39 once and locks 70 once.
